title: Stripe
summary: Problems whose patterns are commonly reported in Stripe coding interviews, from Easy to Hard. Approximate and hand curated, not an official or verified question list.
lesson:
About this list
- Each problem practices a pattern that candidates commonly describe from Stripe technical interviews: HTTP header and string parsing, penalty and schedule optimization, rate limiting, route matching, stateful ledgers and storage reports, expression evaluation, and weighted path finding.
- Problems are grouped Easy, Medium, and Hard so you can warm up on crisp parsing and range logic before tackling multi-part stateful APIs and graph routing.
- The selection is approximate. Interview prompts evolve and vary by team, so treat this track as practical engineering and pattern practice rather than a prediction of what you will be asked.

What to expect
- Candidates often report multi-part, real-world prompts (parsing headers, logs, routes, or financial rules) where part 1 establishes a clean core and parts 2–3 extend it with wildcards, tie-breakers, or extra rules.
- Readable, modular code, careful handling of malformed or edge-case strings, and writing your own verification tests are commonly emphasized over obscure algorithm tricks.
- Exact tie-breaking, case sensitivity, deduplication, and preserving caller order are frequent sources of subtle bugs.

How to prepare
- Read the contract carefully and list every parsing rule, whitespace rule, and tie-breaker before writing code.
- Structure your parsing and matching helpers cleanly so adding a new rule (such as wildcards or fallback precedence) does not require a rewrite.
- Test boundary cases explicitly: empty strings, duplicate entries, case differences, and zero-match fallbacks.
